plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own. Bidding higher risks winning at a price above my value (negative profit), while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities where the second-highest bid is between my bid and value. With value $9, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit regardless of competitors' strategies.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy. This is because you pay the second-highest bid (not your own bid) if you win, so bidding your true value ensures you win whenever the value exceeds the price you'd pay, and never overpay. There's no incentive to shade my bid up or down - truthful bidding maximizes expected profit regardless of other bidders' strategies.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of how many bidders participate or their strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so bidding above your value risks paying more than the item is worth, while bidding below reduces your chance of winning profitable auctions. With my value at $32, I should bid exactly $32 to maximize expected profit.
